players.product: Jenbacher gas engines and gensets (Type 6 / J624 platform; containerized 5 MW units and multi-pack configurations) for behind-the-meter prime and backup power at AI data centers; Jenbacher power-solutions gensets (utility, peaker, biogas); Waukesha gas compression engines; lifecycle services

Adjusted EBITDA $459.9 million (21.3% margin) in 2024 and $401.1 million (19.9%) in 2023; 2025 adjusted segment EBITDA: Equipment $204.6 million (2024: $120.6 million), Services $373.1 million (2024: $373.5 million). Q1 2026: net sales $668.6 million versus $494.0 million in Q1 2025; adjusted EBITDA $122.5 million (18.3% margin) versus $114.0 million (23.1%); Equipment adjusted segment EBITDA $22.9 million versus $28.2 million.
quarterly_data.figure: data center equipment revenue $261.8 million (2025) vs $57.2 million (2024); 2024 net sales $2,159.1 million; Q1 2026 net sales $668.6 million vs $494.0 million; Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA $122.5 million (18.3%)

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus KPIs: equipment order intake $3,884.0 million in 2025 versus $1,349.6 million in 2024 and $910.3 million in 2023, and $1,617.5 million in Q1 2026 versus $652.8 million in Q1 2025. Equipment order backlog $4,780.7 million at March 31, 2026 (December 31, 2025: $3,599.3 million; 2024: $994.1 million; 2023: $650.1 million). Installed base 44 GW (2025), 42 GW (2024), 41 GW (2023); power delivered 3.4 GW in 2025 and 2.5 GW in both 2024 and 2023, 0.7 GW in Q1 2026 versus 0.5 GW. Remaining performance obligations $7,019.7 million at March 31, 2026, with approximately 80% expected to be recognized in the following 24 months ($5,456.8 million at December 31, 2025, approximately 76%); contractual service agreements recognized under the right-to-invoice expedient, which can run 10 years or more, are excluded. Normal book-to-bill cycle for Equipment is 3-12 months but can range up to three years depending on how far ahead customers order and on production-slot availability. Data center equipment order intake rose approximately 16 times from 2020 to 2025; equipment order intake book-to-bill 2.8x. LTM Q1 2026 equipment order intake: data center $2,979M (61%), power solutions $1,522M (31%), compression $348M (7%); LTM Q1 2026 revenue: data center $317M (11%), power solutions $946M (34%), compression $215M (8%), services $1,334M (47%).
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 equipment order intake $1,617.5 million (Q1 2025: $652.8 million); 2025 order intake $3,884.0 million (2024: $1,349.6 million); RPO $7,019.7 million (~80% within 24 months); LTM Q1 2026 data center order intake $2,979M (61%)

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus data center business: approximately 80% of the data center equipment order backlog at December 31, 2025 was associated with prime power applications and the remaining 20% with backup power. The core offering is the containerized Jenbacher Type 6 engine platform, typically deployed as single units (5 MW) or aggregated into standardized multi-pack configurations such as 25 MW; data center customers include colocation operators, energy-as-a-service providers, hyperscalers and land developers. INNIO 'recently partnered with an energy-as-a-service (EaaS) provider to deploy 2.3 GW of advanced power-infrastructure solutions' (provider not named). As of March 31, 2026, approximately 62% of equipment order intake was generated from data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: ~80% prime / 20% backup of data center backlog (end-2025); 2.3 GW EaaS partnership; multi-packs such as 25 MW; ~62% of equipment order intake from data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus customer concentration: Clarke Energy, INNIO's largest (top) indirect account by revenue, accounted for 15.0%, 10.5% and 11.8% of revenue in 2025, 2024 and 2023 (15%, 11% and 12% where rounded in the filing). In the United Kingdom, 98 Type 6 engines were installed together with Clarke Energy to deliver approximately 450 MW of peak power near London.

Prospectus customer concentration (customers not named): top five customers by revenue accounted for approximately 39% of revenue in Q1 2026 and approximately 34%, 27% and 28% in 2025, 2024 and 2023. The financial statements state that one customer accounted for more than 10% of total revenue in each of 2025, 2024 and 2023, with revenue of $395.6 million, $226 million and $238 million, of which 70%, 54% and 57% related to the Equipment segment. The filing says contracts with some large data center customers provide favorable terms such as penalties INNIO owes for delivery delays, equipment non-conformance and equipment failures.
quarterly_data.figure: top five customers ~39% of Q1 2026 revenue; 34% (2025), 27% (2024), 28% (2023); one customer $395.6 million revenue (2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus geography and capex: the revenue mix is shifting toward North America, primarily on data center equipment orders. North America was 39.7% of net sales in Q1 2026 (Q1 2025: 34.0%) and 29.9% in 2025, 26.9% in 2024 and 23.4% in 2023; United States revenue $697.2 million in 2025 versus $495.9 million in 2024 and $346.9 million in 2023 (Q1 2026: $240.3 million versus $143.6 million). Capital expenditures $171.2 million in 2025 (6.5% of revenue, the majority for growth initiatives and funded from operating cash flow, with a significant portion directed to North America) versus $86.6 million in 2024 and $78.2 million in 2023; $51.6 million in Q1 2026 versus $26.9 million. Q1 2026 cash from operating activities $189.0 million versus $24.1 million, driven by higher customer pre-payments on growing equipment order intake; investing cash use rose to $51.4 million, primarily for capacity (mainly machinery and suppliers' assets expansion).
quarterly_data.figure: North America 39.7% of Q1 2026 net sales (2023: 23.4%); US revenue $697.2 million (2025) vs $495.9 million (2024); capex $171.2 million (2025, 6.5% of revenue); Q1 2026 operating cash flow $189.0 million

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus supply and capacity: INNIO relies on a limited number of suppliers, and in some instances a single supplier, for certain equipment and components; steel is the principal raw material in its engines. It uses long-term supply agreements where supplier diversification is not feasible or strategically desirable and with its top suppliers, and works with suppliers on future capacity and regionalization. Capacity is being expanded across engine assembly, component manufacturing and containerization (higher utilization of the Waukesha, Wisconsin and Welland, Ontario facilities, the containerization project in Trenton, New Jersey and new dedicated sites in Texas); the filing flags ramp-up risk at Trenton and Waukesha against committed delivery dates and says supplementing capacity at existing European facilities would be possible only after specific upgrades expected no earlier than 2028.

connects_to.relationship: gas engine power equipment (incl. a containerized solution) for VoltaGrid's energy-as-a-service power business serving data center, industrial, energy and oil & gas customers (customer named by the filer as a significant source of Equipment Order Intake)

contracts.signal: INNIO's prospectus names VoltaGrid, 'a specialized EaaS provider for CNG and power, serving customers across data center, industrial, energy and oil & gas sectors', as a significant source of its Equipment Order Intake: approximately 41%, 14% and 10% of Equipment Order Intake in 2025, 2024 and 2023 (an order-intake share; the filing notes that order intake concentration does not translate directly into the same level of revenue concentration). INNIO has delivered and commissioned a containerized solution deployed in collaboration with VoltaGrid for one of VoltaGrid's major data center customers.
